content: Hello. My background is in computer vision, been interested in lean but haven't done anything with it before. Yesterday I got Claude to make a demo of training a MNIST network using Lean4 and built basic MLP and CNN demos that work end-to-end. I put the code up here: https://github.com/brettkoonce/mnist-lean4 Let me know what you think!
v2: Added better parallelization, scaled to 180 cores on a cloud instance.

Curious if you can add (ask Claude) some theorems of correctness of the algorithms implemented. Looks like there are zero theorems in the repo right now. IMHO (probably spicy) but writing Lean without proofs is just another FP.
Theorems.lean Does some of what I would call consistency checking, then says FloatArray != Lean.Float for the rest iiuc
neat! Lots of sorries, but sounds like there are reasons why proofs can't be completed, bummer.
